description: My name is Shatrah Ddamulira, an aspiring Biomedical Engineer from Uganda, pursuing a Diploma at Kyambogo University. I'm passionate about space medicine, human health in space and developing technologies to monitor and support astronaut health. My interests include software engineering, Python, artificial intelligence and blockchain, particularly their application to healthcare and real-world challenges. I am driven by innovation and technological development in Africa.

details: AstroCare is an open-source web app that helps astronauts understand their own health when ground support is delayed. On a Mars mission a message can take up to 22 minutes each way, and crew members are not doctors, so they often need to make the first decision themselves. Each day the astronaut enters eight readings: heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, temperature, blood sugar, sleep, mood and exercise. AstroCare marks each one as Normal, Watch or Act now, explains it in plain language, and lists what to do next, including when to contact the flight surgeon. It also flags risky combinations, such as a fever with a fast heart rate, and slow trends that a single reading would miss. A tappable body map, an emergency guide and a CSV export for the flight surgeon complete the experience. The body areas and mission settings are organised around the five hazards of human spaceflight used by NASA's Human Research Program. All guidance lives in one rules file so clinicians can review it. It is built with Python and Django and has 30 automated tests. It is a prototype, not a medical device: the screening ranges are unvalidated, the crew data is synthetic, and calibration with NASA data is the next step. Code, tests, documentation and slides were drafted with Claude (Anthropic) and reviewed by the team.
